- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to align with mean reversion.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.67) or neutral (0.00), model often underestimates; adjust upward, especially if recent price is trending up.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +3%+ in 3-5 days), model frequently overshoots in next 5-7 days; apply a “cool-down” correction by reducing forecast by 1-2%.
- If model forecast is consistently above true outcome for 3+ consecutive days, apply downward bias correction (e.g., subtract 0.5–1.5% from next forecast).
- If sentiment is volatile (alternating +/– 0.67), model tends to overfit short-term noise; smooth forecasts by averaging last 3–5 days’ true values.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overpredicts mid-term (days 10–20) when sentiment is bullish; cap forecast at +2% above recent 7-day average.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 days after peak, price drops 2–5%), model tends to ignore it; apply a “reversion buffer” to forecast downward 1–3% for next 3–5 days.
